item.title: Squeeze7z 0.2.2
item.description:
Verification now shows its progress.

  • Fixed: during the last step (verifying the new archive) the row stayed at 0 files until the end, which on a large folder could mean minutes without any sign of life. It now shows the percentage, the files checked out of the total and the time left, like the compression step does.

Copies of 0.2.0 or later offer this update by themselves (Squeeze7z → Check for Updates…). From 0.1.x, download it once by hand.

Requirements: macOS 26 or later, Apple Silicon. The app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized: after the first attempt to open a downloaded copy, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click "Open Anyway". Updates installed by the app do not need this step.

item.title: Squeeze7z 0.2.1
item.description:
Live progress, and large photo archives no longer stall.

  • While a job runs, its row shows the step it is on (extracting, compressing, verifying) with a percentage, the files done out of the total, the file being worked on and the time left for that step.
  • While it compresses, the Saved column shows an estimate in grey (≈) of what the new archive will save against the original. The exact figure replaces it once the archive is verified.
  • Fixed: two large photo archives processed side by side could take most of the Mac's memory and slow to a crawl. Each job now sizes its encoders for its share of the memory. On two 7z archives of JPEG photos (3.1 GB and 10.6 GB), jobs that were still running after 50 minutes now finish in about 3 and 7 minutes.

Copies of 0.2.0 offer this update by themselves (Squeeze7z → Check for Updates…). From 0.1.x, download it once by hand.

Requirements: macOS 26 or later, Apple Silicon. The app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized: after the first attempt to open a downloaded copy, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click "Open Anyway". Updates installed by the app do not need this step.

item.title: Squeeze7z 0.2.0
item.description:
Squeeze7z now updates itself.

  • The app checks GitHub for new versions. On the second launch it asks whether to check automatically; you can change that in Settings → General or check by hand with Squeeze7z → Check for Updates….
  • When a new version is out, it shows what changed, downloads it, and installs it and relaunches when you agree. Updates are signed: the app refuses an archive that was not signed with the project's key.
  • Each Settings tab is now as tall as its rows, so General and Compression no longer need scrolling.

Coming from 0.1.x: this one download is manual, since those versions have no updater. Later versions arrive through the app.

Requirements: macOS 26 or later, Apple Silicon. The app is ad-hoc signed and not notarized: after the first attempt to open a downloaded copy, go to System Settings → Privacy & Security and click "Open Anyway". Updates installed by the app do not need this step.
